text:
Alex: Quick idea — propose we switch to an epochal slicing model for usage metering instead of per-request leases. Anchor all credits/events to epoch_id = floor(ts / EPOCH_LEN).
Maria: can you say more about EPOCH_LEN? 5m? 1h?
Alex: Thinking 1h for compacting and fewer late-arrival merges, but open to shorter. The main win: compaction/gc becomes per-epoch instead of chasing individual claim lifecycles.
Chen: downside: late arrivals that belong to previous epoch require backfill, and we end up with cross-epoch attributions. How do we attach final provenance?
Ravi: we should keep a provenance pointer (event_fingerprint -> epoch_id assigned) and a small sidecar index for late-arrival corrections. That index can be append-only so audits still reconstruct ordering.
Maria: +1 on provenance pointer. Also need to think about tenant fairness — if we batch by epoch we must avoid a tenant busting a single epoch and causing compaction pressure.
Alex: good call. I sketched a hybrid: epoch + shard sequence. Each event gets {epoch_id, shard_bucket, local_seq}. Compaction runs per-epoch+bucket.
Chen: pseudo:
```
EPOCH_LEN = 3600
epoch_id = ts // EPOCH_LEN
bucket = hash(tenant_id) % N
local_seq = assign_monotonic(bucket, epoch_id)
store_key = epoch_id|bucket|local_seq
```
This keeps keys compact and deterministic.
Ravi: how about attribution? currently we rely on tokenlineage sidecar to annotate tokens -> request_id -> tenant. If we move to epoch keys, does attribution still map unambiguously?
Alex: attribution stays the same: attribution records reference store_key. The expensive part is ensuring idempotency for retries across epoch boundaries. If a request spans epoch boundary we canonicalize to the originating epoch (by request start_ts).
Maria: that helps. What about audits that need per-token timestamps for billing windows? If billing wants minute-level chargebacks we lose granularity.
Ravi: billing can still prorate within epoch by storing a small histogram in the claim: per-claim token counts with offsets. We don't store token-by-token. 
Chen: Another thought: introduce a reconciliation pass that runs at epoch+1 which looks for fingerprints in the late-index and merges any corrections into the epoch ledger. That keeps the hot path simple.
Alex: proposed reconciliation flow: 1) ingest writes claim to epoch ledger 2) if late arrival (ts < current_epoch - 1) write to late-index 3) nightly reconciler consumes late-index and emits corrective events + audit logs.
Maria: sounds operationally reasonable. Need SLO for reconciler (how quickly do we close audits?). Also need visibility in Console (per-epoch diffs).
Ravi: auditability: ensure corrective events are first-class and include original_fingerprint, correction_reason, and delta_token_counts. That way an auditor can replay ledger + corrections.
Alex: agree. Also want to avoid an unbounded late-index. We should TTL by max_backfill_window (e.g., 7d) and emit alerts if late-index growth > threshold.
Chen: on storage: compaction will drop per-request payloads but keep provenance pointers and small correction records. That reduces storage by ~4-6x in my estimate.
Maria: ops questions: how do we roll this out? Feature flag per-tenant? Start with non-billing shadow mode?
Alex: rollout plan: shadow-mode (writes both current claim and epoch-claim), run reconciler in dry-run and compare totals, then opt-in small tenants, then ramp.
Ravi: also ensure we can migrate existing compacted ledger to epoch format with a backfill job that emits epochal claims. Might need a stable mapping for old fingerprints.
Chen: agree. Backfill job: scan raw events -> assign epoch keys -> write into epoch ledger with a provenance mapping table. Add a deterministic marker so we don't double-count.
Maria: UI: Console needs per-epoch comparisons, and a flag to show reconciliation corrections. Ops needs alerts for mismatch ratios > 0.1%.
Alex: TL;DR: epochal slicing looks promising for compaction and auditability if we add: provenance pointer, late-index + reconciler, TTL for late-index, deterministic canonicalization for spanning requests, and a shadow rollout.
Ravi: +1. I'd like an RFC that covers failure modes (reconciler outage, double-count risk, cross-epoch request flows).
Chen: I'll draft an RFC with diagrams and a sample migration plan.
Maria: also include a small cost estimate and query patterns for Console.
Alex: great — Chen, can you own the RFC? I'll schedule a 30m follow-up sync next week.
ingest-bot: Deploy finished: metering-spike v0.3 -> prod-staging :rocket:
Maria: thanks — ping me when the draft is up, I have a few audit testcases. :eyes:
Alex: ack, will post link to RFC thread.
